overview: Guoquan Food is China's leading at-home hotpot and barbecue meal-ingredient brand, operating under the 'Guoquan Shihui' (鍋圈食匯) banner through a nationwide network of over 12,000 instant-retail stores as of mid-2026, more than 99.9% of which are franchised. The company positions itself as a 'community central kitchen,' selling hotpot soup bases, meatballs, shrimp paste, meat, vegetables, beverages and other ready-to-eat/heat/cook ingredients so households can replicate restaurant-style hotpot and barbecue meals at home. It is a Shanghai-headquartered, RMB-reporting company listed on HKEX (H-shares, HKD-quoted) since November 2023.

business_model.summary: Guoquan is fundamentally a wholesale supplier to its own franchise network, not a franchise-fee collector: it does not charge or rely on franchise fees, and derives substantially all revenue from selling branded food products to franchisees, who then operate stores and sell to consumers. Profitability therefore depends on wholesale volume to franchisees, product mix/gross margin, and the pace of store network expansion -- not recurring royalty streams.

revenue_streams.name: Sales to franchisees (wholesale of meal products)
Other sales channels (enterprise/wholesale customers, direct-to-consumer, online/Douyin)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B (franchisees who operate retail stores), supplemented by enterprise/wholesale customers (food wholesalers, supermarkets, restaurants) and growing direct-to-consumer online sales (Guoquan APP, WeChat mini-program, Douyin livestreaming, Meituan/Ele.me delivery)
business_model.geographic_mix: Essentially 100% Mainland China; stores span 31 provinces/autonomous regions/municipalities with a deliberate strategic focus on township and lower-tier/rural markets. Nascent overseas pilot (Hong Kong SAR store trial) announced for 2026 as a first step toward international expansion.

main_competitors: Lanxiong (懶熊) and other hotpot-ingredient 'supermarket' chains (鼎匯豐, 九品鍋, 自然饞, 火鍋物語)
Yihai International (Haidilao's condiment/ready-to-eat supplier, retail hotpot bases and sauces under Haidilao and Hot Kid brands)
Supermarket chains launching competing 'store-in-store' hotpot-ingredient counters at lower price points (e.g., Wumart tie-up undercutting franchisee margins)
Traditional wet markets and e-commerce grocery/fresh-food platforms (Meituan, Ele.me, Pinduoduo, Douyin e-commerce) selling similar prepared ingredients directly to consumers
Restaurant-based hotpot chains (Haidilao, Xiabuxiabu, Jiumaojiu) that compete for the same at-home-vs-dine-out spending but operate a different (dine-in) business model
competitive_position.market_position: Largest and most geographically extensive branded player in China's at-home hotpot/barbecue ingredient retail niche, with first-mover scale advantages (7 self-operated ingredient factories, ~21 digitalized central warehouses) built over roughly a decade; the category itself, however, has low barriers to entry and has attracted many regional copycat chains since 2020-2021.

moat_factors.description: 'One-product-one-factory' vertically integrated production plus a national digitalized warehouse/logistics network gives bargaining power with upstream suppliers and next-day fulfillment that smaller regional chains struggle to match.

moat_factors.factor: Store network density and brand recognition
moat_factors.description: Over 12,000 stores nationwide, heavily weighted to township/county markets, create a first-mover density advantage and local brand recall ('community central kitchen' positioning) that is costly for new entrants to replicate quickly.

82 million registered members (H1 2026) generating 73% of sales, prepaid card balances, and a multi-platform content/e-commerce engine (Douyin GMV +97% YoY) build switching costs and repeat purchase behavior at the consumer level.

Franchisees fund their own store buildout and inventory, letting Guoquan scale store count without heavy capex, but also means the company has limited direct control over in-store execution and franchisee economics, and does not earn high-margin recurring franchise-fee income.

The category itself (hotpot ingredient retail) has low technical/regulatory barriers; competitors can replicate the store format relatively cheaply, limiting pricing power and compressing margins over time.

weaknesses: No franchise-fee/royalty income stream -- the model depends entirely on wholesale volume and gross margin, so profitability is exposed to input cost inflation and competitive discounting
Thin and compressing gross margins (21.5-22.8% range) typical of a low-differentiation packaged/prepared food wholesaler rather than a branded consumer products company
Heavy reliance on franchisee goodwill and execution quality in 11,500+ independently run stores, with limited direct operating leverage over the in-store consumer experience
Vulnerable to being undercut by supermarket 'store-in-store' competing formats and larger retailers entering the category at lower price points
Single-market (China) concentration with only a nascent, unproven overseas pilot

growth_drivers: Continued store network expansion, especially the 'four-store' format strategy (large township stores, large community stores, Guoquan camping stores, Guoquan stir-fry stores) targeting lower-tier/rural markets under a 'food equality' positioning
Upgrade of existing community stores into larger-format stores with broader SKU assortment, which management says lifts per-store sales efficiency
Rapid growth of social-commerce/livestreaming channel (Douyin GMV up 75-117% YoY in recent periods) converting online traffic into offline store visits
Membership ecosystem deepening (82 million members, AI-personalized marketing, prepaid card balances) driving repurchase rates (members now ~73% of total sales)
New 'Guoquan Farm' premium/fresh-ingredient product line, delivering very high GMV growth (>600% YoY) off a small base
Vertical integration/industrial buildout (new Danzhou, Hainan production base; seven ingredient factories) expected to lower unit costs and widen procurement bargaining power
Early-stage overseas expansion pilot in Hong Kong as a first step to exporting the brand
AI/digital supply-chain investment (smart production scheduling, inventory monitoring) targeted at offsetting margin pressure from commodity costs and competition

business.risk: Intensifying competition in a low-barrier category
business.description: Numerous regional hotpot-ingredient chains (Lanxiong and others) and supermarket 'store-in-store' formats are undercutting prices, which management and sell-side analysts explicitly link to margin compression concerns.

Revenue depends on franchisees remaining profitable enough to keep buying inventory and opening new stores; the company does not disclose detailed per-store economics, and a prior prospectus disclosed closure rates around 2.8-3.0% in 2021-2022, with management guiding to a closure rate below 4% for H2 2026.
Management explicitly attributed H1 2026 gross margin decline (22.1% to 21.5% YoY) partly to lower-margin non-traditional products (e.g., durian pulp SKUs) introduced to diversify the portfolio.

Revenue is overwhelmingly tied to hotpot/barbecue ingredient sales to franchisees; a shift in consumer dining-out vs. at-home preference (as occurred in 2023 when revenue fell ~15% amid a dine-out recovery) can materially swing results.

financial.description: Cash used in operating activities was RMB102.4 million in H1 2026 (vs. RMB29.0 million used in H1 2025), despite rising reported net income -- a working-capital/receivables divergence that merits scrutiny on earnings quality.

Interest-bearing borrowings rose 139% to RMB332.8 million as of 30 June 2026 from RMB139.0 million at FY2025-end, pushing the gearing ratio from 6.7% to 12.0% in six months; the company has no interest-rate hedging policy.
Cash is held mainly in RMB and some HKD; the company does not use derivatives to hedge foreign-exchange risk, though direct exposure is limited given the almost entirely domestic business.

regulatory.description: As a nationwide prepared-food manufacturer/distributor, Guoquan is subject to PRC food safety law and could face reputational and financial damage from any quality incident across its large franchise network.

Operating 11,500+ franchised stores exposes the company to PRC franchise regulations and potential disputes with franchisees (the company disclosed losing a supplier-related import-agency lawsuit costing RMB11.8 million in H1 2026).

macro.description: Management's own chairperson statement cites 'the trend toward rational consumption... deepening' and a restructuring channel/traffic landscape in China, reflecting a cautious, value-seeking consumer backdrop that squeezes both volumes and pricing.

Gross margin pressure was partly attributed to rising prices of certain raw materials; as a food manufacturer/wholesaler, Guoquan has limited ability to pass through cost increases given intense category competition.

A rebound in restaurant dining (as seen in 2023) directly substitutes away from at-home hotpot ingredient purchases, making the business sensitive to the broader post-pandemic normalization of Chinese consumer dining habits.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: At-home hotpot/prepared-ingredient retail in China grew rapidly post-COVID but has since matured into a crowded, lower-growth, increasingly price-competitive category; township/rural market penetration remains a structural growth pocket given lower existing store density and a government/consumer narrative around 'consumption downgrade' favoring value-for-money options.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical/counter-cyclical to dine-out spending: at-home meal retail tends to benefit when consumers trade down from restaurant dining (value-seeking behavior) but can lose share when dine-out confidence recovers, as occurred in 2023.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (business is not capital-intensive at the parent level since franchisees fund store buildout), but rising short-term borrowings and the absence of hedging create some exposure to RMB funding costs.

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results released: revenue up 21.8% YoY to RMB3,946.9 million, net profit up 12.1% YoY to RMB213.2 million, but operating cash flow swung to a RMB102.4 million outflow and gross margin compressed to 21.5% from 22.1%; shares continued to fall despite the growth, down roughly 60% year-to-date by some reports.

Mixed sell-side reaction to interim results: SPDB cut its price target from HK$3.10 to HK$2.20, while CMB International, CICC, Huatai and Guotai Haitong maintained Buy/Outperform ratings with targets of HK$2.60-3.84, reflecting a wide dispersion in views on margin trajectory.

Board proposed changing the use of Global Offering net proceeds and extending the expected timeline for full utilization (subject to shareholder approval), as roughly HK$293 million (65%) of IPO proceeds remained unutilized as of 30 June 2026.

Controlling shareholders (including other major holders) extended a share lock-up commitment by six months past the original 6 May 2026 expiry, a move the company framed as signaling confidence but which followed a reported ~70% decline from the stock's 52-week high.

FY2025 annual results: revenue RMB7,810.0 million (+20.7% YoY), net profit RMB453.9 million (+88.2% YoY), net margin improved to 5.8% from 3.7%; store count reached 11,566 (net addition of 1,416 stores, including 1,004 net new township stores); total dividend of RMB0.1097/share plus RMB183.9 million of share buybacks during the year.

Store count grew from 9,660 (H1 2024) to 10,150 (FY2024) to 10,400 (H1 2025) to 11,566 (FY2025) to 12,198 (H1 2026); Douyin-channel GMV growth accelerated sharply (+75.3% in FY2025, +97.2% in H1 2026) as social-commerce becomes a larger growth driver.

items.target: exceed 13,100 stores (net addition of over 1,534 stores for FY2026)
items.vs_prior: new guidance (consistent with multi-year expansion cadence)
items.notes: Management expects H2 2026 new stores to predominantly adopt the large-store format.
No comparable prior-year disclosure found in extracted filings; historical closure rates were 2.8-3.0% in 2021-2022 per prospectus data.
Tied to the strategy of upgrading community stores into larger formats with broader SKU assortment.
Up from 82.0 million at H1 2026 (already +63.0% YoY) and 64.9 million at FY2025-end.

items.vs_prior: maintained directionally, though qualitative ('stable growth') rather than quantified
items.notes: Core operating margin was 5.7% in H1 2026 vs. 5.9% in H1 2025, i.e. already showing slight compression; FY2025 core operating profit grew 48.2% YoY to RMB460.7 million, so FY2026 guidance implies a much slower growth rate than the prior year's pace.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairperson Yang Mingchao's FY2025 statement emphasized 'long-term mindset,' balancing scale expansion with operational quality amid a Chinese consumer backdrop of 'rational consumption' and reconstituting channel/traffic dynamics. H1 2026 management discussion attributed gross margin softness to new lower-margin product introductions and raw material cost inflation, while highlighting supply-chain efficiency gains as a partial offset. Management reiterated no plans for derivative FX/interest-rate hedging and described liquidity as sufficient for daily operations and capex needs despite the operating cash outflow.

bull_case: Market-leading scale (12,000+ stores, 7 owned factories, ~21 digital warehouses) gives Guoquan a structural cost and distribution advantage over smaller regional hotpot-ingredient chains as the category consolidates
Underpenetrated township/rural markets offer a long runway for store net-adds (1,000+ net new township stores per year) with a differentiated 'food equality' value proposition
Fast-growing digital/social-commerce flywheel (Douyin GMV +75-117% YoY, 82 million members generating ~73% of sales) is building a lower-cost customer acquisition and retention engine

Capital-light franchise wholesale model requires minimal capex for store growth, supporting continued shareholder returns (FY2025 dividends + buybacks totaled ~RMB474 million) even amid margin pressure

Shares have already de-rated sharply (reportedly down ~60-70% from highs), and several brokers (CMB International, CICC, Huatai, Guotai Haitong) maintain Buy ratings, implying meaningful potential re-rating if margin concerns prove transitory
bear_case: Low barriers to entry in hotpot-ingredient retail have invited a wave of copycat chains and supermarket store-in-store formats that are structurally compressing gross margins (down from 22.8% in H1 2024 to 21.5% in H1 2026)

Operating cash flow has turned sharply negative (RMB102.4 million outflow in H1 2026) even as reported net income grows, raising questions about receivables/working-capital quality behind the headline profit growth

No franchise-fee/royalty revenue model means the business captures only wholesale product margin, leaving it structurally more exposed to commodity cost inflation and price competition than a true franchisor
Rising leverage (gearing ratio from 6.7% to 12.0% in six months, interest-bearing debt +139%) alongside no FX/rate hedging adds financial risk at a time operating cash generation has weakened

Revenue is entirely dependent on Chinese consumers' at-home-vs-dine-out spending mix, which proved volatile in 2023 when a dine-out recovery drove a ~15% revenue decline; a repeat of that dynamic combined with current margin pressure could compound negative sentiment
